title: Private deployments: VPC & On-Prem deployment, packaging, day-2 ops, upgrade and rollback guidance
author: Marina Alvarez
content:
Overview

This document consolidates Redwood Inference's recommended reference architectures, deployment checklists, on-prem packaging guidance, day-2 operational procedures, and deterministic upgrade/rollback procedures for Private Deployments (VPC and on-prem). It is intended for SREs, platform engineers, and customer success engineers who install, operate, and support customer private stacks.

Scope
- Applies to: Private deployments delivered as VPC-hosted control plane + customer-managed inference fleet, and fully on-prem/self-hosted packages.
- Included topics: network & IAM requirements, reference architectures, packaging formats, step-by-step deploys, day-2 ops (monitoring, backups, scaling), upgrade & rollback runbooks, and the customer requirements library.

Quick summary of responsibilities
- Redwood: provide control plane, signed releases, Helm charts / OCI images, security patches, and upgrade orchestration guidance.
- Customer: provide compute, networking, DNS, secrets/KMS, and cluster maintenance for on-prem and VPC private agents.
- Redwood support & CSE: validation, canary upgrades coordination, and incident escalation.

Reference architectures
1) VPC Mode (recommended starting point)
   - Topology: Customer VPC hosts inference clusters (EKS/GKE/AKS or equivalent) + private subnets for worker nodes. A lightweight Redwood agent runs in the VPC to register capacity with the Redwood control plane over a secure mTLS tunnel.
   - Key components:
     - Control-plane connector (agent) - outbound-only TLS, port 443; uses customer-provided certs or Redwood-issued short-lived certs.
     - Model-serving pool - GPU nodes in private subnets; autoscaling with Karpenter/HPA.
     - Data plane storage - NFS / S3-compatible object storage with signed credentials for model artifacts and KV caches.
   - SLO targets (customer configurable, recommended defaults):
     - Control-plane connection availability: 99.9% monthly
     - Worker process availability: 99% per cluster
     - Inference latency: P95 <= 250ms for token sizes <= 128 (dependent on hardware & model)

2) On-Prem Mode (air-gapped / isolated sites)
   - Topology: Fully self-contained bundle: local control plane (optional), orchestration manifests, OCI image mirror, and installer. No outbound connections required beyond internal registries.
   - Packaging: tarball with signed Helm charts, model artifact bundle, and an operator for lifecycle tasks.

Pre-deployment checklist (network, security, quotas)
- Networking
  - Ensure private subnets with route tables for worker nodes.
  - NAT gateway or proxy for outbound access (VPC agent) OR preseed images/manifests for air-gapped installs.
  - DNS: wildcard entry for internal API endpoint (redwood-inference.local or customer chosen).
- Identity & Access
  - KMS: provide key alias/ARN if integrating with Redwood KMS for model encryption.
  - Service accounts with least privilege: allow S3 access limited to model buckets, ECR/GCR pull, and cluster admin for initial install (revoke later).
- Quotas & capacity
  - GPU quota validated: recommended baseline for pilot = 4x A10G / A100 equivalents depending on model size.
  - PV size: 200Gi per node group for model caches and logs (adjust by workload).

Packaging & installers
- VPC mode: Helm chart + values.yaml published as OCI artifact. Charts include: control-plane-agent, inference-worker (daemonset/statefulset), cache-proxy, and node-exporter config.
- On-prem: Signed tarball (sha256) including: Helm charts, offline image bundle (oci-archive), installer.sh, postinstall validator, and a minimal Prometheus + Grafana stack for local observability.
- Example values snippet (values.yaml):

  agent:
    image: ghcr.redwood-inference.com/agent:2026.11.1
    replicas: 2
    tls: { use_customer_certs: true }
  worker:
    nodeSelector: { gpu: "true" }
    resources: { requests: { cpu: "2000m", memory: "8Gi" } }

- Notes: All images are signed with Redwood's cosign key. Verify with: cosign verify --key <pubkey> <image-ref>

Deployment procedure - VPC (high level)
1) Validate prerequisites: run the preflight script (scripts/preflight.sh) which checks cluster permissions, quotas, and network reachability.
2) Install ingress & cert-manager if not present.
3) Add Redwood Helm OCI repo and pull chart:
   - helm repo add redwood-helm oci://ghcr.redwood-inference.com/charts
   - helm pull oci://ghcr.redwood-inference.com/charts/private-agent --version 2026.11.1 --untar
4) Apply values.yaml and install:
   - kubectl create namespace redwood-private
   - helm upgrade --install redwood-agent private-agent/ -n redwood-private -f values.yaml
5) Validate: ensure agent reports to control plane via CLI (redwoodctl agent status) and check /var/log/redwood/agent.log for errors.

Deployment procedure - On-Prem (air-gapped)
1) Mirror images to the private registry: registry-mirror.sh --bundle redwood-offline-2026-11-1.tar.gz --target-registry my-registry.local
2) Run installer: sudo ./installer.sh --namespace redwood-private --registry my-registry.local --skip-scc
3) Run postinstall validator: ./validate-postinstall.sh --endpoint https://redwood-internal.local:8443

Day-2 operations
- Monitoring & alerting
  - Default dashboards: inference latency, token throughput, KV cache hit rate, GPU utilization, pod restart rate.
  - Alert thresholds (recommended):
    - GPU memory >= 90% for > 5m -> severity P2
    - Agent offline for > 10m -> severity P1 (redundant agent recommended)
    - Error rate >= 1% of requests in 5m -> severity P2
- Backups & model artifacts
  - Snapshot model buckets daily; retention 30 days. Use lifecycle policies to rotate older model artifacts.
- Scaling
  - Autoscale policy example (Karpenter suggestion): scale-with-gpu-utilization >= 70% triggers new provisioner. Tune based on observed P95 latency.
- Regular maintenance
  - Weekly: rotate agent certificates if using customer-managed certs, prune images older than 90 days, check disk usage.
  - Monthly: run Canary test suite (suite/canary-latency.sh) to detect inference regressions.

Upgrade & rollback procedure (controlled, safe path)
- Principles: always stage upgrades in a staging cluster, run canary traffic against a small percentage of nodes, capture metrics and golden traces, and have a tested automatic rollback.

Upgrade steps (operator/engineer)
1) Prepare release artifact and verify signatures: cosign verify --key redwood.pub <image>
2) Stage: deploy to staging cluster using helm upgrade --install redwood --namespace redwood-private -f staging-values.yaml
3) Canary: mark 10% of worker nodes with label redwood-canary=true; deploy worker canary image: kubectl set image ds/inference-worker inference=... --record -l redwood-canary=true
4) Run automated validation (canary-latency.sh and canary-quality-check.py). Pass criteria: P95 latency within 10% of baseline AND 99th-percentile output similarity > 99% on the eval prompts.
5) Rollout: if canary passes, use a rolling upgrade with maxUnavailable=1 and surge=1. Monitor for 30m.
6) Finalize: bump version in cluster manifest and notify stakeholders.

Rollback procedure (if metrics fail)
1) Trigger immediate rollback: helm rollback redwood-agent <previous_revision> -n redwood-private
2) Mark cluster as degraded in incident tracker, run full traffic rebalancing to old nodes, and escalate to oncall.
3) Postmortem: collect prometheus metrics, agent logs, and canary traces. Follow the incident postmortem template.

Testing and validation
- Integration tests: preflight, canary latency, and model-quality evals are part of every release.
- Acceptance tests: listed in the customer requirements library section below; run automatically in CI for private packaging builds.

Customer requirements library (selected entries)
| Requirement ID | Requirement | Rationale | Acceptance test |
| RQ-001 | Private outbound-only control-plane connection | Customers prefer no inbound firewall rules | Preflight validates outbound TLS to redwood-control.redwood-inference.com:443 |
| RQ-012 | KMS integration for model encryption | Regulatory requirement for some customers | SRE can decrypt a test artifact using provided KMS alias |
| RQ-023 | Air-gapped install with OCI mirror | Large enterprises require offline installs | Installer completes with --offline flag and smoke tests pass |
| RQ-034 | Auditable upgrade trace | Compliance: must show upgrade steps and hashes | Helm release history and cosign verification stored in audit bucket |

Oncall & ownership
- Primary owner: eng-private-deployments team (pager: #eng-private-oncall).
- When to page: agent offline > 10m, model-serving pod restarts > 3x in 5m, or rollback triggered.
- Escalation path: oncall -> SRE lead -> CSE (customer success engineer) -> Eng product owner.

Appendices
A. Useful CLI snippets
- Check agent status: redwoodctl agent status --cluster my-cluster
- View recent errors: kubectl -n redwood-private logs -l app=redwood-agent --since=30m
- Force rollback: helm rollback redwood-agent 2 -n redwood-private

B. Suggested observability panels
- Cluster summary: total GPUs, active workers, average GPU utilization, 95th latency
- Model-quality panel: canary-pass-rate, similarity-score per model, regression alerts
